items.title: Russia Hits Kyiv In Massive Missile And Drone Attack
items.description: Russia launched 41 missiles and 125 drones in a massive overnight attack on Ukraine, with Kyiv as the main target. Ukrainian officials said it was Russia's largest use of ballistic missiles since the start of the full-scale invasion. At least one person was killed and 16 were injured.

items.title: Russian Strike on Kharkiv Suburbs Kills Three, Injures 20
items.description: Russian forces attacked the suburbs of Kharkiv on Sunday, July 19, resulting in three civilian deaths and 20 people injured. items.title: At least 50 Malian soldiers killed in rebel-jihadist attack
items.description: At least 50 Malian soldiers were killed and dozens more were taken prisoner in an attack by Tuareg separatists and jihadists, local sources said told AFP on Sunday.

items.title: Russia launches largest ballistic missile attack on Kyiv since start of war
items.description: Ukraine is particularly vulnerable to ballistic missile attacks due to a shortage of Patriot air defence munitions.

items.title: NY mayor in talks over whether to arrest Netanyahu at upcoming UN summit
items.description: In an interview with the 'New York Times,' Mayor Zohran Mamdani called Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu a 'war criminal' who 'belongs in The Hague.' He is currently discussing options with the city's legal team to determine his authority to enforce arrest warrants against foreign leaders.

items.title: Gaza officials say several killed in Israeli strike
items.description: Palestinian health and civil defense officials said at least eight people were killed while attending a funeral. Israel's military said it had struck a "terrorist cell" from the Islamic Jihad militant group.

items.title: Hunger deepens for displaced families in Sudan’s El Obeid
items.description: UN humanitarians working in war-torn Sudan on Friday highlighted rapidly growing needs among the more than 100,000 displaced people now sheltering in camps in the city of El Obeid.

items.title: Pro-Kremlin Blogger Arrested for ‘War Fakes’ Months After Denouncing Putin
items.description: In March, Ilya Remeslo shocked both supporters and critics when he publicly denounced President Vladimir Putin in a scathing manifesto.
